title: Chapter 47 — Trade Psychology
intro: How trade professionals think, decide, and evaluate vendors — the psychology behind B2B loyalty.

sections.title: How Trade Buyers Decide
sections.content:
Trade buyers — builders, designers, contractors — evaluate vendors on a completely different axis than retail customers. Retail customers buy on emotion and justify with logic. Trade buyers buy on reliability and justify with economics.

The trade buyer's hierarchy of needs: first, do not make me look bad in front of my client. Second, deliver when you say you will. Third, provide accurate specs and pricing. Fourth, be responsive when I need you. Price is fifth — not first. A builder will pay 5 percent more to a supplier who never misses a delivery over a cheaper supplier who is unreliable.

Understand this hierarchy and you understand trade selling. Every action you take should reinforce the top four before you ever discuss price.

sections.title: Trust Accumulation
sections.content:
Trust in trade relationships accumulates slowly and collapses instantly. Ten perfect deliveries build trust. One missed delivery can destroy it.

The compound effect works in your favour: each successful project adds to the trust balance. After 5 successful projects, the builder stops checking your quotes line by line. After 10, they stop getting competing quotes. After 20, they recommend you to other builders. That is the compound interest of reliability.

But the opposite is also true. One wrong product delivered to a job site — where the plumber, electrician, and cabinetmaker are all waiting — costs the builder a day of labour across multiple trades. They will remember that cost long after they forget every perfect delivery you made.

sections.title: The Loyalty Threshold
sections.content:
Trade loyalty has a threshold effect. Below the threshold, the account is price-sensitive and shops around. Above it, they are relationship-locked and resistant to competitor pitches.

The threshold is usually 5-8 successful projects. Before that, you are being evaluated. After that, you are infrastructure. The strategic implication: invest heavily in the first 5 projects with any new trade account. Over-deliver on speed, accuracy, and communication. That early investment pays dividends for years.
